server-modes-12.title: How should beginners choose a server?
server-modes-12.text: Choose PvE to learn gathering and building: players cannot attack one another, and bases with a Tool Cupboard cannot be raided or destroyed by other players. Choose PvP for combat and raiding. Before joining, check resource rates, wipe frequency and the No PC tag, which means PC players are not allowed on that server.

newbie-servers-105.title: Why has my newbie server disappeared?
newbie-servers-105.text: Newbie servers are temporary learning environments. When their opening period ends, they are permanently removed from the list along with the wipe and cannot be restored. Use them to learn the basics rather than as a server for long-term progress.

server-wipe-8.title: What is a wipe, and where can I check its time?
server-wipe-8.text: A wipe regularly resets server data, clearing buildings, loot and debris from the map for a new survival cycle. In the lobby, open the server list and select the server you want to join. Its details show the creation time and the scheduled time of the next wipe.

solo-duo-trio-248.title: What limits apply on Solo, Duo and Trio servers?
solo-duo-trio-248.text: SOLO, DUO and TRIO limit groups to one, two and three players respectively. The limits also apply to Tool Cupboard authorization and code-lock users. Once full, a lock may refuse a friend even with the correct code. Changing the code or picking up and replacing the door clears the user list; players must then enter the code again. Teaming beyond the limit breaks these servers' rules.

base-upkeep-245.title: Why is my base upkeep getting more expensive?
base-upkeep-245.text: On PvP servers, more structural pieces increase the upkeep surcharge; the largest size bracket can cost twice the base amount. Authorizing more than four players in the cupboard adds a further surcharge. Doors and hatches need upkeep but do not count toward the size bracket. PvE has no such surcharges. Check the cupboard's daily cost for the resources currently required.

building-privileges-191.title: Why can't I build despite having cupboard authorization?
building-privileges-191.text: A cupboard's build zone follows foundations, walls and floors rather than forming a fixed circle around the cupboard. Where several protected zones overlap, the building containing the oldest structural piece determines building permission. Authorization in another nearby cupboard may therefore be insufficient. Walk around and watch the building status indicator to find the boundary.

merge-buildings-190.title: How can separated buildings be merged again?
merge-buildings-190.text: Restoring full side-to-side contact between structural pieces lets the system treat them as one building again. This usually works for a base that was originally connected and later damaged; separately started buildings are difficult to align precisely. After merging, one cupboard and one build zone remain, and the extra cupboard in the absorbed section is removed.

rebuild-debris-200.title: Why can't I immediately replace a destroyed wall?
rebuild-debris-200.text: Destroyed building pieces briefly leave debris that blocks new construction in the same spot. Wait for the construction-blocked countdown to end; the official guide gives about 30 seconds. For some walls, the debris may clear sooner if the supporting pieces are also destroyed.

fence-snapping-209.title: How can I reduce gaps between fences?
fence-snapping-209.text: When placing fences, adjacent sections now snap together and align automatically. This makes a continuous perimeter easier to build and reduces gaps enemies can peek or shoot through. The source describes alignment during placement; it does not say that existing gaps repair themselves.

signal-airdrop-249.title: How do I call an airdrop with a signal flare gun?
signal-airdrop-249.text: The signal flare gun is found only in loot and cannot be crafted. Fire toward open sky at least 45 degrees above the horizon, avoiding roofs, bridges and rock faces. After a successful shot, the plane arrives in roughly one to two minutes and the drop lands near the firing position. Other players may notice the signal, so choose somewhere you can defend while waiting.

first-day-progression.title: Your first day: make tools, then build a small home
first-day-progression.text: Start with wood, stone and food, make basic gathering tools, then choose a resource-accessible spot with fewer passing players for a small home. Gather materials before building so you do not run out halfway. Once you have storage, take only essentials outside and return to deposit a good haul. Invest in expensive gear and major expansion after gathering and storage are reliable.

gather-hit-markers-116.title: Follow the markers when chopping trees and mining
gather-hit-markers-116.text: With ordinary tools, hit a tree once, then aim the next strike at the red trunk marker for more resources and faster felling. Stone and ore nodes show a glowing spot that moves after a successful hit. Locate it again after each hit instead of holding attack on the same spot.

workbench-research-path-243.title: Select your target technology to see the full research cost
workbench-research-path-243.text: Select the equipment you want in the technology tree, even if prerequisites remain locked. The screen shows the remaining scrap cost of the entire path. Confirming researches the missing prerequisites and the target together. Check the total before spending. Actual research requires a workbench within about five metres; opening the tree farther away is view-only and spends nothing.

solo-base-core-upgrades.title: Solo building: strengthen the core before the outer layers
solo-base-core-upgrades.text: With limited solo resources, put the Tool Cupboard deep inside the core. Upgrade the core structures to stone first, then gradually to metal, while strengthening the doors. Add outer defensive layers once the core is secure. Tuck furnaces into corners to leave walking room. The author's design uses an entrance buffer room to reduce direct exposure of the interior when checking outside.

spread-base-loot-83.title: Spread valuables around your base to limit losses from one breach
spread-base-loot-83.text: Add defensive layers outside important rooms so attackers must break through more obstacles. Store valuables in different parts of the base instead of risking everything at a single breach. The Tool Cupboard remains a priority: keep it protected and locked. Spreading loot reduces the damage from one breach; it does not guarantee that supplies survive a complete raid.

turret-placement-247.title: Aim turrets at doors and corridors, then check ammunition
turret-placement-247.text: While placing a turret, use the translucent sector on the ground to aim it at a doorway or a corridor enemies must cross. Load the correct ammunition and check the remaining rounds when restocking the cupboard: an empty turret will not fire. Teammates need authorization in the cupboard covering the turret or may become targets. Crafting also consumes the actual weapon in the recipe, so include it in your budget.

backup-supplies-84.title: Keep backup supplies elsewhere in case your base falls
backup-supplies-84.text: Besides defending your main base, keep basic supplies in another hidden location so a bad night does not force a complete restart. Travel with others when carrying valuable cargo. This preparation addresses what happens after the main base falls: supplies spread inside it can still all be lost, while a separate reserve offers another route to recovery.

raid-preparation.title: Check four equipment groups before a raid
raid-preparation.text: Before leaving, check your primary weapon and spare ammunition, backup weapon, breaching rockets or C4, and armor and supplies. Prepare medkits, bandages, water and sleeping bags, and repair worn gear first. Do not take all your most valuable items at once; keep emergency equipment in reserve. Consider retaliation when choosing targets: a base close to home is not necessarily a good choice.

player-shop-stock-79.title: Check player shops on the map before travelling
player-shop-stock-79.text: Open the map and select a player shop icon to check goods and prices before making the trip. The marker disappears when the shop sells out. When running your own shop, place the vending machine within a cupboard's zone or others may take goods and earnings from the back. Empty the earnings storage regularly; trades stop when it is full.

quarry-collection-80.title: Collect quarry output regularly after adding fuel
quarry-collection-80.text: After unlocking the Mining Quarry blueprint, gather the materials and craft it on the server; buying it in the main shop does not give you a finished machine. Place it and add fuel to produce stone and ores. Running it makes noise that attracts enemies, and other players may take resources left inside. Protect the surroundings and collect the output promptly.
